Obvious comparisons to another space-themed hidden role game aside, Goose Goose Duck stands easily on its own with a reasonable game balance (as of this writing some of the roles are still being tweaked), interesting maps, and a sense of humor that pervades the entire experience.

Being currently in early access, public lobbies can be a bit of a hit or miss experience, but private lobbies have been nothing but hilarious and fun. Highly recommend for fans of the genre.

Ok, here's the pros and cons; Pros are that this game can be played with multiple people, (up to 16 as of now), there are plenty of public games and probably one in three are filled with decent non-toxic players. There are a ton of roles and there are more coming in pretty regularly so far. The graphics aren't too intense so it works on not so up to date computers, (like mine cough cough), and the game is entertaining even without all the roles or with fewer players. If you've played modded Among Us, you already know how to play for the most part. It's also free, so there's that. Cons: You can easily earn silver coins by playing the game, and gold coins can be earned too but more slowly. You need those coins to unlock outfits for your Goose/Duck which can mean spending real money if you want something specific. The other 2 of the 3 lobbies will be toxic, I'm just warning you beforehand. Use the report buttons if someone is actually breaking the rules, cheating or just being a terrible person in general. That's it, that's all I've got. Goodluck and GG!

This social game has the most unlikable game community (you would be sourcing from a discord server) I ever stumbled upon - and I used to play at some point almost every competitive game released in two decades including the most notorious offenders. What gives GGD the cake is not the upfront "solo mid" hostility of your average competitive multiplayer game but seething passive-aggressive mentality and unabridged hostility of a twitter heard communication behind almost every single conversation you would be forced into by "normal people who play casual games" and make up the surface web society you drafted from GGD discord channel for a private game.
This game may be an option to play with your friends (although there are better alternatives I don't know if I can mention in a steam review) but without 10 plus your best chums to get your lobby going you would be pressed into playing with what social network communication has to offer.
